links.note: The Bogomils began in Bulgaria in the 900s. The same movement lived on in the Balkans and in Byzantium after 1054. The Croatian historian Franjo Rački, writing in 1869 from Greek sources, found a Bogomil group in the Greek capital by the mid-1000s. Its leader Basil, tried under the emperor Alexios I, said he had led it for over forty years.

prose_changes.old: Around 1173 a rich merchant of Lyon named Valdes gave away his property, had parts of Scripture translated into the language people actually spoke, and began preaching in the streets. His confession of faith was entirely orthodox. What he would not do was stop preaching without a license, and in 1184 the bull Ad abolendam condemned him and his followers for exactly that. Driven out of the cities, the movement survived in the Alpine valleys between France and Italy for three and a half centuries of intermittent persecution, with its own traveling ministers and its own books. In 1532 its representatives met the Reformers at Chanforan and threw in with the Reformed tradition. Which is why a single line of protest can be followed from twelfth-century Lyon into the Reformation without a break.
prose_changes.new: Around 1173 a rich merchant of Lyon named Valdes gave away his property. He had parts of Scripture put into the language people actually spoke, and he began preaching in the streets. His confession of faith was wholly orthodox. What he would not do was stop preaching without a license, and in 1184 the bull Ad abolendam condemned him and his followers for exactly that. Driven out of the cities, the movement held on in the Alpine valleys between France and Italy. It lasted through three and a half centuries of on-and-off persecution, with its own traveling ministers and its own books. In 1532 its leaders met the Reformers at Chanforan and threw in with the Reformed churches.
